When you ask “what happens under the hood?” the real story spans multiple layers:

1) DNS lookup process visualized
- Name resolution (and caching) determines which IP your client targets.
- Changing your IP / querying DNS can shift where traffic lands, affecting latency and reachability.
- TTL + resolver caches create “stale vs fresh” trade-offs.

2) How internet routing works
- After you have an IP, routers forward packets hop-by-hop.
- Routing tables + metrics drive “best path” selection.
- Convergence and transient inconsistencies can cause short-lived blackholes or reroutes.

3) TCP vs UDP socket programming trade-offs
- TCP: connection establishment, ordered delivery, retransmissions, and flow/congestion control (more state, more reliability).
- UDP: minimal overhead and lower latency, but app-layer handling is required (reordering, loss recovery, etc.).

4) Production architecture lesson (pattern that scales)
- Observability-first: log DNS resolutions, target IPs, RTT, retransmits/timeouts.
- Resilience: retries with backoff, circuit breaking, and fallback to cached answers.
- Clear contracts: separate “transport guarantees” from “application correctness.”
